summary: Autoscaler starve window during shortwave burst + tenant coldstart causing transient GPU attach failures
description:
Issue summary: BrightLens reported intermittent p50->p99 spikes and request failures for reserved dedicated pool during a 30m window on 2026-03-10. Impact: customer-facing degraded throughput and ~15% of requests returning 504/attach-timeout for short-lived streams, causing elevated error rates in their production app.

Observed timeline: 2026-03-10 09:10-09:40 UTC saw a shortwave burst of many short-lived coldstart streams (median 700ms) from a BrightLens job. Autoscaler did not provision additional slots quickly; allocator logs show slots temporarily held by background prefetch and one noisy tenant. Result was transient GPU attach timeouts and cascading retries.

Why this is customer-impacting: Dedicated pool expectation for BrightLens (reserved) is predictable throughput and low failed attach rate. The combination of a sudden high fanout of short sessions plus delayed attach/eviction recovery led to perceived capacity loss and increased latency.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) In a reserved pool with mixed long and many short streams, script a shortwave burst of 8k short-lived streams over 5-10 minutes targeting a single tenant slot group.
2) Ensure background KV-prefetch sweep runs concurrently.
3) Observe allocator attach latencies, autoscaler decisions, and per-tenant slot occupancy.
4) Measure p50/p99 token latency and failed attach rate.

Notes: Reproduction requires reserved GPU pool and ability to create many short sessions. We reproduced in staging with a simulated tenant.
logs: Selected excerpts: allocator.log[2026-03-10T09:12:14Z] WARN attach_timeout tenant=brightlens slot_id=pool-23-7 delta=3.1s; autoscaler.log[2026-03-10T09:12:20Z] INFO scale_down_candidate window_mean=0.02 but burst_detected=true; prefetcher.log[2026-03-10T09:11:58Z] INFO kv_prefetch hold_slot=pool-23-7 duration=4.2s. Stacktrace snippets around attach timeouts included socket timeout during nvlink handshake and repeated backoff. Full logs on internal S3: s3://redwood-ops/logs/SUP-358642/
investigation_notes:
Initial triage: Support reproduced a short-lived p99 spike in staging by simulating the exact burst profile. Observed that autoscaler smoothing window (30s) suppressed aggressive scale-up because recent average appeared low. Meanwhile, a noisy tenant's prefetcher held several slots for 3-5s each, leading to slot attach queueing.

Hypothesis A: Autoscaler smoothing + cooldown prevented timely scale-up during shortwave bursts.
Hypothesis B: Background prefetch and a noisy tenant's long-lived connection pattern caused ephemeral slot blocking rather than true GPU exhaustion.

Telemetry: Correlated allocator queue depth increase with prefetch sweeps and a single tenant (tenant-842) that had a burst of healthcheck/logging connections. No evidence of driver crashes or GPU OOM. NVLink latencies briefly increased but within acceptable ranges.

SRE action: Instrumented autoscaler to emit burst_detected flag and added a high-frequency probe on attach queue length. Confirmed that enabling burst detection would have triggered an earlier scale-up in the reproduced scenario.

root_cause_summary: A confluence of autoscaler smoothing (designed to avoid oscillation) and slot-holding background work from a noisy tenant caused short-lived attach queueing. The autoscaler did not register the shortwave burst quickly enough to add capacity, resulting in temporary GPU attach failures and elevated p99 latency. No hardware or driver faults detected.
workaround: Immediate: Applied temporary capacity bump for the customer's reserved pool (added 2 GPU equivalents) and throttled prefetcher tasks for the noisy tenant. Customer reverted their ingest job to a slower ramp as an interim measure.
resolution: Mitigation deployed: temporary pool bump + prefetch throttle. Engineering merged autoscaler change to reduce smoothing sensitivity for detected shortwave bursts (PR github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/314). A permanent autoscaler improvement and a tenant-side guidance doc were scheduled. Awaiting postmortem and customer acceptance before closing.

notes_for_records: This ticket highlights an operational edge case for reserved pools: heuristics that intentionally damp autoscaler reactivity can interact badly with short, high-fanout coldstart patterns and background system tasks. Consider policy parity between dedicated/private pools for aggressive short-burst handling.
